title: AI-assisted CT risk score retains mortality discrimination in a later COVID-19 cohort
summary: A five-variable model combining demographic data, oxygen saturation and automatically extracted CT measurements distinguished recorded mortality in a later COVID-19 cohort. Developed from 1,125 first-wave patients, AI-SCoRE achieved a reported AUC of 0.808 in 213 second-wave patients. This supports a bounded clinical prognostic validation, without demonstrated treatment benefit or proof that the predictor was locked before validation outcomes accrued.
ai_technology: Pretrained U-Net lung segmentation with quantitative CT feature extraction, logistic risk modeling and CART risk binning
organization: Vita-Salute San Raffaele University; IRCCS San Raffaele Scientific Institute

evidence.tested: A multicenter first-wave dataset was reduced from 1,575 enrolled patients to 1,125 complete records, including 292 deaths. Repeated train/test splits and repeated cross-validation compared candidate models and selected a five-variable logistic model. Pretrained learned segmentation enabled automated lung measurements. A later, prospectively collected single-center cohort of 213 patients, including 31 deaths, yielded AUC 0.808 with reported 95% confidence interval 0.740–0.877.
evidence.unknown: Prospective cohort collection does not establish that the model and thresholds were fixed before its outcomes were known. Complete-case selection, different pandemic waves, one-center later validation and historical treatment conditions limit transportability. The paper inconsistently describes 213 versus 214 validation patients and presents four low-risk deaths as 1.8% without a clearly appropriate low-risk denominator; those percentages and post-hoc exclusions are not adopted here. Supplemental acquisition/endpoint details were not independently read. No causal CT mechanism, intervention benefit or current clinical utility is established.
evidence.ai_role: Pretrained neural segmentation converted patient CT scans into quantitative lung features used with clinical variables in the represented mortality score; learned risk modeling and binning enabled the patient-outcome discrimination analysis.

source_review.scope: Read primary front identity/date, clinical study design, modeling and segmentation Methods, cohort/model/later-wave mortality Results and limitations. Supplemental Methods were not independently read. Later cohort collection was prospective; temporal predictor locking was not established. Exact original article front DOI/title and fresh PubMed primary relationship metadata checked.
